text: 🎬 Taron Egerton is the most wanted man in London. Not by the police. Director Jonathan Schey inverts the predatory-dating dynamic entirely: the women stalk, Egerton's "nice guy" Adam is the target. Sharp satirical premise, backed by Film4, StudioCanal, and LuckyChap, and clearly self-aware about every inch of its title. The title stays. Good. Egerton playing a murky, likeable-but-not charmer is smarter casting than it first appears, and this kind of dark British comedy with actual teeth is exactly what Film4 does best. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Mike McFarland is gone. The voice of an old man who never actually grew old. Mike McFarland passed away at 56 from glioblastoma, leaving behind a run that shaped how an entire generation heard anime in English. He joined Funimation in the late '90s and never left, voicing Master Roshi across every corner of the Dragon Ball Z universe, plus Buggy the Clown in One Piece . 56 years old. He started playing a lecherous immortal hermit at around 30. What gets me is how much he did with Roshi in Dragon Ball Super's Tournament of Power arc. A character who could've coasted on cheap comic relief ended up landing genuine weight. That was McFarland finding something real inside the joke. Voice acting that invisible is the hardest kind. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🍿 Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen is the most unsettling casting of the year 📆 Estreno: September 25, 2025 🎭 Género: #TrueCrime #Drama ✈️ Add to watchlist Lance Oppenheim built his rep on docs that feel fiction-adjacent (Ren Faire, Spermworld), so flipping that lens onto To Catch a Predator is a genuinely smart move. Robert Pattinson doesn't do an impression; he plays the hunger behind the performance, that barely-contained thrill of a man who knows the cameras love him. The ghillie-suit moment in the clip is peak TCAP absurdity. Oppenheim keeps it deadpan. That instinct is exactly why this works.
